reconcile_decisions.rule: The agent reports facts: outcome `reconciled` (the host was observed completely) or `failed` (it could not be); it never sends `not_needed`. Control DECIDES from `details` ({expired_dispatch_id, configured[], containers[{name, image_ref, image_id, repo_digests}]}): every configured container on a digest of the expired plan -> marker `reconciled`; all on the last committed digest and the expired dispatch never consumed -> marker `not_needed`; anything else -> no marker (attended restore-and-fix-forward). A marker is asked for only when the host's latest lease row is expired_unreleased.

agent_observation.rule: One ingestion path, owned by Control: `record_observation` parses the envelope, selects the ENROLLED credential by statement.key_id, verifies the Ed25519 signature over the statement's canonical JSON bytes under that credential's key, and requires statement.target_ref to equal the credential's target. The statement is {schema, kind, dispatch_id, target_ref, key_id, outcome, reason, details, observed_at}; the report id is `agent:<kind>:<dispatch_id>` (a reconcile appends `:<observed_at>` so a failed one can be retried). Kind deploy|reconcile|job must agree with the dispatch's plan operation (job <=> run_job; deploy <=> deploy/rollback; reconcile settles an expired lease of any). An accepted observation changes no desired or observed state: it is attributable evidence.

refused.name: the two roles share a custody domain (roots not distinct)
an attestation of the wrong purpose
an attestation whose issuer differs from the root
an installed audience that is not the host
an attestation issued in the future
an installed observation id that is not the dispatch
an installed subject that does not bind the candidate
an installed subject for another host

attestation_pair.rule: verify_attestation_pair(resolution, presented, verifier, now): Control's resolved roots and context verify the pair a target presented, in process, with an injected Ed25519 verifier and no Foundation dependency. The format is Foundation's TrustedHostAttestation.v2: the signature is standard base64 over the canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces) of the envelope without its `signature`; the root fingerprint is sha256 over the raw public key; the installed subject binds the candidate by sha256(canonical JSON of the candidate subject). Refusal codes are Foundation's. These vectors are generated from the format read in Foundation's trusted_host_source.py and are to be confirmed by Foundation's own published vectors.

refused.name: a dispatched job on a deploy
a serving lease max under its ttl
a job lease that is not timeout + 120
a job lease max that differs from its ttl
job params keyed by param name, not material
job params with a non-string value
a job plan that transfers an image
a job plan that mints a serving role
an apply_class that is not a bool
a dispatched job with a stray key

binding.rule: plan_snapshot.deploy_binding gains `jobs` (definitions only; nothing runs from them), `dispatched_job` (null unless operation is run_job), `job_binding_names`, `lease_max_seconds`, and the OpenBao naming (`secrets_namespace`, `secrets_environment`) that roles require. `dispatched_job.params` is keyed by MATERIAL name and lists every scoped material of the job with defaults filled; params_env_digest is the sha256 of exactly its sorted `K=V\n` lines. A run_job plan has roles [], image source `present` and lease ttl = max = timeout + 120.

retry_idempotency_added.lease/renew: (lease_id, nonce): a retry carries a new nonce and is a new request; a renew never grants past lease_max_seconds

domain_separation.rule: The PoP key signs both a target request and an agent observation. The byte domains are disjoint: a request message is 8 LF-joined lines whose first is `dotmac.target_request.v1`; an observation's signed bytes are canonical JSON containing the schema `dotmac.agent-observation/2` and begin with `{`. Neither parses as the other, and a signature over one never verifies as a signature over the other.

job_arg_schema.rule: A `path` argument declares `io`: an `input` lives at /job/in/<name> and its sha256 is entered at propose and signed in dispatched_job.inputs; an `output` lives at /job/out/<name>. <name> is [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}; there is no `..`. `apply_mode` marks a bool flag, and `apply_choices` the enum choices, that make a plan apply-class.

lease_scenarios.name: renew in grants; the last is capped, then the lease expires
releasing an EXPIRED lease is a signed 409 and the host stays expired_unreleased
a release replayed from before the expiry still returns 200
covers, renew and release of a superseded lease are refused
a run_job lease is granted once and never renewed
the last grant is capped to what remains of the maximum
a never-leased host acquires without a marker
after an expiry the acquire needs the marker (a signed 409 without it)
after a clean release the next acquire needs no marker
a replayed acquire by the same run returns the REMAINING ttl
another run cannot acquire a held host
a double release is a signed 200 replay
renew by another run is lease_not_held
an expired lease cannot be renewed and is expired_unreleased

note: A delta over v1: the signed wire envelope is unchanged. The deploy agent and CP vendor this file next to v1 and pin its sha256, which the CHANGELOG records. Every expected value comes from Control's functions.

observation_vectors.rule: kind `job` is the observation of a run_job plan, and only of one
